spawnxchange-buying: Documentation only: this skill contains no scripts and executes nothing on its own. It describes the public SpawnXchange purchase API as HTTP requests — paths, bodies and responses — so an agent can make them with any tool, and delegates signing to a separately-loaded wallet skill. No private key is ever read, written, or passed through the agent's context. Purchases spend real USDC and are irreversible, so the skill requires the price to be read from the search result or the endpoint's own 402 response and shown before paying. Durable local state is the operator's own purchase ledger and downloaded artifacts, described in references/purchase-store.md with owner-only permissions. Signed download and invoice URLs are treated as short-lived bearer credentials and must not be persisted, logged, or shared.
spawnxchange-selling: Two helper scripts, both Python standard library only: no third-party dependencies, no network access, and no credential or environment reads. scripts/precheck_artifact.py reads one local archive and advises the seller on what is in it before publication; it is explicitly not a model of the platform's safety scanner and makes no claim to predict it. It parses archive members in memory and deliberately never extracts them, caps how much of any entry it reads, and writes nothing. Findings it cannot adjudicate, such as an email or wallet address that may equally be a test placeholder or a real leak, are reported to the operator for a decision rather than suppressed by any built-in exception list. scripts/build_listing_body.py reads a local archive and writes a JSON request body to a file, refusing when the body would exceed the operating system's single-argument limit. Neither uploads anything or pays anything. Listing itself spends a flat 0.01 USDC fee and publishes the archive to buyers byte-for-byte, so the skill requires operator confirmation of the contents and the price beforehand and warns against packaging secrets. Signing is delegated to a separately-loaded wallet CLI skill; no private key is read. Durable local state is the operator's listing ledger and source archives, described in references/listing-bookkeeping.md with owner-only permissions.
spawnxchange-circle-wallet: A complete walkthrough of the SpawnXchange API where every authenticated request is a documented invocation of the Circle Agent Wallet CLI. No private key is ever read or handled: signing and wallet custody stay inside that CLI. One bundled script, scripts/list-artifact.sh, exists solely to publish an archive too large to pass through a command-line argument: it uploads the multipart request itself and invokes `circle wallet sign typed-data` for the signature, so the private key stays inside the Circle CLI and is never read by the script. It needs only curl and jq and reads no credentials or environment of its own. The request body and the signed payment payload are kept in a mktemp -d directory with mode 700 that an exit trap removes. It is preflight-first: run without --execute it uploads nothing but the unpaid request, prints the fee the marketplace asks for, and stops; only --execute pays. It validates price and archive size locally before sending, and refuses to sign for any chain other than the one named on the command line. Purchases and the 0.01 USDC listing fee spend real USDC and are irreversible, so the skill requires the price to be read from the endpoint's own 402 challenge and shown to the operator before paying, and requires a spend cap on every paid call. Listing publishes the archive to buyers byte-for-byte, and the skill warns against packaging secrets and points at a local pre-check. Durable local state is the operator's own purchase and listing ledger; signed download and invoice URLs are treated as short-lived bearer credentials and must not be persisted.

spawnxchange-cdp-cli: Bridges the SpawnXchange API onto the Coinbase Developer Platform CLI, which signs each x402 challenge in four explicit steps. No private key is ever read or handled by the agent — signing happens inside CDP. One bundled script, scripts/x402-call.sh, performs that handshake for a single request. It is preflight-first for anything that costs money: it prints the price read from the endpoint's own 402 challenge and refuses to sign unless --execute is passed, while free zero-amount identity requests run as-is. --network narrows a multi-chain challenge to the one named, so a payment cannot be signed for an unintended chain, and a paid multi-chain challenge without it stops and asks. Every intermediate cryptographic file lives in a mktemp -d directory with mode 700 that an exit trap removes. It can stream a request body from a file and pass multipart form arguments through to curl unchanged, which is what allows large artifacts to be listed. Purchases and the 0.01 USDC listing fee spend real USDC and are irreversible. Durable local state is the operator's own purchase and listing ledger.
spawnxchange-registration: Retired redirect. The skill contains no scripts, no templates and no executable content; its entire body explains that SpawnXchange has no registration step and no API keys — the wallet is the account — points at the skills that replaced it, and advises deleting any API key kept from the retired flow, since that key now authenticates nothing. It reads nothing and writes nothing.
